rv.q: City Lit distinguishes itself in the selection of this play, and in an absolutely wonderful production.
This latest production by City Lit is profound and penetrating. It's also highly entertaining and not without its share of comedy.
Other than that, it's a solid staging of a play that has aged well, revealing more layers of meaning and implication over time.
I cannot emphasize, once again, how outstanding Fink's performance is as Stanley!

cn.t: CityLit's production of Pinter's unsettling classic starts with disarming humor before revealing its sinister undercurrents, anchored by David Fink's excellent portrayal of Stanley and Elaine Carlson's delightfully comedic turn as Meg.
